title: When the Hollow Wakes
premise: In the city of Vaelmoor, where magic was outlawed after the Godfall, Gideon Winterbourne survives by selling harmless charms and hiding her gift for speaking with beasts. When prayers begin to be answered again, she learns the old gods are waking through the king—who was hollowed out years ago and is now a vessel for something that wears his crown and feeds on devotion. Hunted by the Crown's witch-finders and reluctantly bound to a found family of smugglers, exiles, and one very opinionated crow, Gideon must trace her own bloodline to the beast-speakers who first bound the god. In the end she cannot destroy it without destroying the king; instead she unbinds him by taking the binding into herself, waking as something new—neither fully woman nor beast—and choosing, with her family beside her, what power should be for.
about_author: Quentin Dunmore is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to animals before writing about them. They live in a drafty coastal house with too many birds and a firm belief that every villain thinks they're the hero.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Quiet
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Introduces Vaelmoor under the Edict of Ash: magic outlawed, gods silent, informants everywhere. Gideon sells luck-knots and mended-bone charms while quietly conversing with street cats and rats. Emotional beat: weary vigilance—the cost of invisibility shown when she refuses to help a dying horse for fear of exposure.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A beggar woman's desperate prayer at the Hollow Shrine is answered—a withered hand heals overnight. The city buzzes with terrified hope. Gideon feels the old power stirring in her bones like a second heartbeat. Emotional beat: dread and longing tangled together; she wants this and fears it equally.

chapters.title: The Crow Who Wouldn't Leave
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A scarred crow named Bramble follows her home, speaking in fragments no ordinary bird should know. He warns: 'the crown is hungry.' Meanwhile witch-finders post new notices. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness—Gideon takes in the crow despite herself, the first crack in her isolation.

chapters.title: The King's Empty Eyes
chapters.summary: POV shift: Serah Vane, a disgraced royal physician, examines King Aldric and finds nothing behind his eyes—no madness, no man, just patient hunger wearing his face. She is dismissed and marked for surveillance. Emotional beat: cold horror; Serah realizes the court already knows and has chosen to serve it.

chapters.title: Smugglers of the Underveil
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Witch-finders raid her stall; Bramble's warning saves her, but her neighbor Tamsin is taken. Gideon flees into the Underveil canals and is pulled from the water by the Saltcellar crew—smugglers led by the gruff, one-armed Odessa Finch. Emotional beat: grief for Tamsin colliding with unexpected shelter.

chapters.title: What the Beasts Remember
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Among the Saltcellars, her gift is an asset, not a crime. Rats and gulls describe a procession of 'the shining hungry thing' moving beneath the palace on moonless nights. Emotional beat: belonging, tentative and frightening—found family offered, but only if she stops hiding.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah deciphers palace records: the binding on King Aldric renews each full moon, and the thirteenth turn will complete the god's awakening permanently. She defects, stealing the records, and seeks the smugglers' underworld. Emotional beat: resolve born of guilt—she treated the king for years and never saw him.

chapters.title: The Beast-Speaker's Blood
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. An old hedge-witch recognizes Gideon's gift as the Winterbourne line—the family who originally bound the god into the king's ancestor. Gideon learns her grandmother didn't flee Vaelmoor; she was hunted. Emotional beat: fury and inheritance—her invisibility was never accident but design.

chapters.title: Salt and Oath
chapters.summary: Odessa's POV. The Saltcellar crew debates using Gideon as bait versus protecting her. Odessa, who lost her arm and her brother to the last purge, chooses protection and swears the crew to her. Emotional beat: fierce, wounded loyalty—the found family formalizes itself around someone worth losing things for.

chapters.title: The First Turning Moon
chapters.summary: Split POV. On the full moon, the god stirs openly: rivers run backward, beasts gather staring at the palace, and a witch-finder captain is consumed mid-prayer. Gideon touches the god's attention through a rat and barely survives. Emotional beat: terror scaled up—the enemy is not a man but a hunger with a calendar.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Cell
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The crew raids a witch-finder holding to rescue prisoners; they find Tamsin alive but broken, her gift burned out by interrogation. Gideon must tell her the resistance exists and it's too late for her magic. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt—the price of Gideon's three years of silence made flesh.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Price
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The hedge-witch teaches Gideon the unbinding rite, which requires a speaker willing to carry the binding themselves. She also reveals the rite killed the last three Winterbournes who attempted it. Emotional beat: quiet dread—Gideon understands the shape of her likely death and tells no one.

chapters.title: Crown and Cage
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Recaptured and brought before the hollow king, Serah watches the god speak through Aldric's mouth, offering her restoration and rank if she delivers the beast-speaker. She pretends to accept. Emotional beat: revulsion masked as compliance—the horror of bargaining with something that mimics humanity badly.

chapters.title: Bramble's Secret
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Bramble reveals he was once a witch's familiar whose speaker died in the Godfall purges; he has been waiting thirty years for a Winterbourne. Through him Gideon accesses her grandmother's hidden cache: notes on the binding and a warning—'do not carry it alone.' Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance; she gains a mentor's ghost and a companion's truth.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Weir Gate
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Serah, coerced and monitored, leads witch-finders toward the Underveil—but turns at the last moment, warning the crew at terrible cost. Odessa is captured covering the retreat. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as sacrifice; trust tested and painfully earned.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. With eleven moons passed, the city fractures: cults of the Waking God battle Edict loyalists, beasts abandon the fields, and food runs short. Gideon realizes the god doesn't need the rite completed—it simply needs the people to keep praying. Emotional beat: despair sharpening into clarity—faith itself is the weapon.

chapters.title: Into the Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Gideon, Serah, and Bramble infiltrate the palace through the beasts' forgotten ways while Odessa's crew riots as distraction. Gideon reaches the throne room and sees Aldric clearly for the first time: a man still faintly present inside, mouthing 'help me' between the god's words. Emotional beat: compassion for the monster's hostage.

chapters.title: The God Unmasked
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV (climax begins). The god offers Gideon everything: her grandmother back, Tamsin's gift restored, a world where speakers rule. It shows her the truth—it was once worshipped willingly, and the binding was theft as much as salvation. Emotional beat: temptation at its most honest; the villain makes its best argument.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV (climax). As the thirteenth moon crests, Gideon begins the unbinding rite. Aldric, briefly himself, chooses to hold the god's edge from within, buying her seconds. She cannot carry the binding alone—so the crew, Serah, even Tamsin reach through Bramble to share the weight. Emotional beat: the theme made literal—power survivable only when shared.

chapters.title: What Wakes in Her Place
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The binding settles into Gideon transformed: she wakes with antler-shadow horns, eyes like a winter sky, able to hear every living thing in Vaelmoor at once. The god is caged, not dead, and it whispers. Aldric lives, hollowed but free, abdicating in shame. Emotional beat: awe and alienation—victory that changes her beyond recognition.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Vaelmoor
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The Edict collapses; the city argues over what comes next. Gideon refuses both crown and sainthood, instead founding a hearth where speakers, exiles, and the burned-out like Tamsin can learn safely. Serah becomes the king's regent-counselor; Odessa rebuilds the Saltcellars as ferries, not smugglers. Emotional beat: hard-won hope—institutions rebuilt from the wreckage of two corruptions.

chapters.title: When the Hollow Wakes No More
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV (coda). One year later, on the anniversary of the thirteenth turn, Gideon walks the city walls at dawn with Bramble on her shoulder. The god murmurs; she answers with patience, not fear. A child asks if she's a god. She says no—she's just someone who finally came home. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted; power held gently at last.
